title: System Design Interview Study Plan for Interns & New-Grads
description: A structured, ground-up System Design curriculum tailored for internship and new-grad candidates. Focuses on core building blocks, trade-offs, horizontal scaling, and end-to-end design practice.
goal: Master distributed system fundamentals and trade-off analysis to pass Internship and New-Grad System Design technical interviews.
subject: System Design & Distributed Systems
audience: CS student or intern with basic SQL, REST APIs, OS, networking, and Python knowledge

sources.title: Core Concepts for System Design Interviews (Hello Interview)
Load Balancing for System Design Interviews Explained (DEV Community)

modules.title: Module 1: Foundations of Networking & Single-Server Request Flow
modules.summary: Understand how client requests travel across DNS, TCP/UDP, HTTP protocols, and Layer 4 vs Layer 7 load balancers before entering distributed complexity.

modules.title: Module 2: Core Building Blocks & Horizontal Scaling
modules.summary: Learn to scale out a web application from 1k to 1M users using stateless web tiers, load balancing algorithms, Redis caching, and database read replicas.

modules.title: Module 3: Advanced Distributed Systems & Data Tier Scaling
modules.summary: Master database sharding, consistent hashing with virtual nodes, asynchronous message queues (Kafka/SQS), and CAP/PACELC consistency trade-offs.

modules.title: Module 4: The 6-Step Interview Execution Framework
modules.summary: Learn the 45-minute technical interview framework: requirement scoping, back-of-the-envelope calculations, API design, high-level blueprinting, and bottleneck defense.

modules.title: Module 5: Applied System Design Case Studies & Mock Practice
modules.summary: Hands-on, worked-example practice designing classic architectures: URL Shorteners, News Feeds, Video Streaming (YouTube), and High-Concurrency Event Booking (Ticketmaster).

tasks.title: DNS Resolution & Single-Server Request Flow
tasks.description: Trace the step-by-step journey of a URL request from browser local cache to ISP recursive resolvers, TLD/Root DNS, and A/CNAME records, down to single-server execution limits.
objectives: Explain recursive vs authoritative DNS resolution steps
Identify hardware bottlenecks in single-server architectures
tradeoffs: High TTL: maximum DNS cache hits vs Low TTL: rapid IP failover
verificationQuestions: What happens when a browser DNS cache misses?
Why is a single server both a capacity bottleneck and SPOF?

tasks.title: Transport & Application Protocols: TCP, UDP, REST, gRPC
tasks.description: Compare transport reliability (TCP 3-way handshake vs UDP) and client-server API protocols (REST JSON vs gRPC Protocol Buffers over HTTP/2).
objectives: Select appropriate protocols for web APIs vs internal microservices
Explain gRPC efficiency over JSON over REST
tradeoffs: REST: human-readable and standard vs gRPC: ultra-low binary payload and high throughput
verificationQuestions: When would you choose UDP over TCP?
Why is gRPC preferred for internal microservice communication?

tasks.title: Real-Time Communication: WebSockets vs SSE vs Polling
tasks.description: Examine real-time pushing mechanics: Short/Long Polling overhead, Server-Sent Events (SSE) unidirectional streaming, and WebSockets full-duplex persistent connections.
objectives: Choose between SSE and WebSockets based on traffic directionality
Explain HTTP Upgrade header mechanics for WebSockets
tradeoffs: SSE: simple HTTP unidirectional push vs WebSockets: bidirectional full-duplex stateful overhead
verificationQuestions: Why are WebSockets ideal for collaborative editing like Google Docs?
When is SSE preferred over WebSockets?

tasks.title: Layer 4 vs Layer 7 Load Balancing Breakdown
tasks.description: Analyze transport-layer (L4 TCP/UDP 4-tuple) vs application-layer (L7 HTTP payload) load balancing, TLS termination, and path-based routing.
objectives: Differentiate L4 packet NAT forwarding from L7 content inspection
Design path-based routing rules for microservices
tradeoffs: L4: high throughput and low CPU cost vs L7: intelligent path routing and TLS termination at higher CPU cost
verificationQuestions: What packet details does an L4 load balancer inspect?
Why is L7 required for routing requests based on HTTP cookies or paths?

resources.title: Load Balancing for System Design Interviews Explained

tasks.title: Web & Data Tier Separation and Database Paradigm Selection
tasks.description: Separate web application logic from persistent database storage. Compare Relational SQL (ACID, normalized joins) vs NoSQL paradigms (Key-Value, Document, Wide-Column).
objectives: Decouple application execution from persistent storage
Select SQL vs NoSQL based on ACID and schema flexibility needs
tradeoffs: SQL: strict consistency and complex joins vs NoSQL: flexible schema, fast key lookups, and easy horizontal scaling
verificationQuestions: Why split web servers and database servers onto distinct machines?
When is a NoSQL Key-Value store preferred over a SQL database?

resources.title: SQL vs NoSQL and Web/Data Separation

tasks.title: Load Balancer Algorithms & Health Checking
tasks.description: Evaluate Round Robin, Weighted Round Robin, Least Connections, and Power of Two Choices algorithms. Configure active HTTP health checks and active-passive failover pairs.
objectives: Match load balancing algorithms to variable vs uniform request costs
Eliminate load balancer single points of failure using virtual IP failover
tradeoffs: Round Robin: simple but fails under non-uniform workloads vs Least Connections: optimal load tracking at higher state tracking cost
verificationQuestions: Why does Round Robin fail when request processing times vary significantly?
How do active health checks prevent routing traffic to dead backends?

resources.title: Load Balancing Algorithms and Health Probes

tasks.title: Stateless Web Tier Architecture & Shared Session Stores
tasks.description: Eliminate sticky session dependencies by moving user session state out of local web server RAM into a shared in-memory Redis cluster, enabling elastic auto-scaling.
objectives: Design a stateless web tier capable of auto-scaling
Store user session state in shared key-value stores
tradeoffs: Sticky sessions: simple local memory lookups but uneven load distribution vs Stateless: elastic auto-scaling with network call overhead to session store
verificationQuestions: Why do sticky sessions break elastic auto-scaling?
How does storing session state in Redis allow any web server to handle any request?

tasks.title: In-Memory Caching (Redis) & Cache-Aside Pattern
tasks.description: Implement in-memory caching to achieve sub-10ms database reads. Master Cache-Aside, Write-Through, Write-Back patterns, TTL expiration, and LRU eviction policies.
objectives: Implement Cache-Aside read/write logic in Python pseudocode
Select LRU vs LFU eviction policies based on access patterns
tradeoffs: Cache-Aside: lazy loading and stale data risk vs Write-Through: strict write consistency at higher write latency
verificationQuestions: Walk through the step-by-step logic of a Cache-Aside read request.
What is the risk of setting no TTL on cached keys?

tasks.title: Cache Stampede Mitigation & CDN Media Acceleration
tasks.description: Prevent cache stampede (thundering herd) failures using distributed mutex locks and probabilistic early expiration. Offloading static assets (images, JS, CSS) to CDN edge nodes.
objectives: Mitigate cache stampedes when hot keys expire
Leverage CDNs to offload static bandwidth from web servers
tradeoffs: Direct server assets: origin server bandwidth bottleneck vs CDN edge caching: global low latency with edge cache invalidation complexity
verificationQuestions: How does a hot key expiration trigger a cache stampede on the database?
Why should static images and scripts be served from a CDN instead of app servers?

tasks.title: Database Replication: Leader-Follower (Master-Slave)
tasks.description: Scale database read capacity by implementing Leader-Follower replication. Master handles all writes, while multiple Read Replicas serve read queries via async binary logs.
objectives: Configure read replicas to scale read-heavy workloads
Analyze replication lag and read-after-write consistency issues
tradeoffs: Synchronous replication: zero data loss at high write latency vs Asynchronous replication: low write latency with replication lag and stale reads
verificationQuestions: Why can asynchronous read replicas return stale data immediately after a write?
How do you ensure a user sees their own updated profile image immediately after uploading?

tasks.title: Scaling Progression Review & System Architecture Map
tasks.description: Synthesize the 1k to 1M user architectural progression. Review how DNS, Load Balancers, Stateless Web Servers, Redis Caches, CDNs, and Read Replicas assemble into a cohesive system.
objectives: Draw the complete multi-tier system architecture diagram
Identify bottlenecks at each scale threshold
verificationQuestions: Walk through the exact request path for a cached vs uncached user request in a scaled system.
At what user traffic scale do read replicas become necessary?

resources.title: ByteByteGo System Scaling Blueprint
resources.section: Single Server to Millions of Users

tasks.title: Database Sharding & Horizontal Partitioning
tasks.description: Partition large database tables horizontally across multiple database nodes when write volume or dataset size exceeds a single machine capacity. Select shard keys and mitigate hotspots.
objectives: Design a database sharding scheme using a specific shard key
Identify risks of cross-shard joins and celebrity hotspot keys
tradeoffs: Single DB: simple queries and joins vs Sharded DB: massive write throughput and storage capacity at the cost of complex cross-shard queries
verificationQuestions: Why does selecting an ill-fitted shard key (like country code) create hotspot shards?
How do you handle queries that need data spanning multiple shards?

tasks.title: Consistent Hashing & Virtual Nodes (vnodes)
tasks.description: Master consistent hash rings to assign keys to dynamic server nodes without re-mapping the entire cluster when nodes scale or crash. Utilize Virtual Nodes (vnodes) for uniform distribution.
objectives: Explain why modulo hashing (hash(key) % N) breaks during cluster resizing
Trace key assignment and node addition on a consistent hash ring with vnodes
tradeoffs: Modulo hashing: 90%+ key remapping on node change vs Consistent hashing: only 1/N keys remapped on node change
verificationQuestions: Why does adding 1 node to a modulo-hashed cache cluster cause a cache stampede?
How do virtual nodes prevent a single neighbor node from taking 100% of a failed node traffic?

tasks.title: Asynchronous Processing & Distributed Message Queues
tasks.description: Decouple synchronous HTTP response flows from long-running background tasks (video encoding, email delivery, payments) using durable Message Queues (Kafka, RabbitMQ, AWS SQS).
objectives: Architect Producer/Consumer message queue workflows
Buffer high write traffic spikes to protect downstream databases
tradeoffs: Synchronous processing: immediate confirmation at high request latency vs Asynchronous MQ: instant HTTP response with eventual background task completion
verificationQuestions: Why should heavy image processing be handled asynchronously via a queue?
How does a message queue level out a 10x traffic write spike?

tasks.title: Distributed Consistency: CAP & PACELC Theorems
tasks.description: Analyze fundamental distributed trade-offs. CAP Theorem (Consistency vs Availability during Partitions) and PACELC Extension (Latency vs Consistency during normal state).
objectives: Classify systems as CP (Strong Consistency) or AP (High Availability)
Apply PACELC trade-offs to databases like DynamoDB vs PostgreSQL
tradeoffs: CP: return error during partition to guarantee accuracy vs AP: return stale data during partition to guarantee availability
verificationQuestions: Why is a banking ledger classified as a CP system?
What does the PACELC theorem evaluate that CAP ignores during normal non-partitioned operation?

tasks.title: Blob / Object Storage (AWS S3) & Direct Client Uploads
tasks.description: Store unstructured media files (images, videos, PDFs) using Object Storage (S3) instead of relational databases. Implement pre-signed URLs for direct client uploads.
objectives: Architect S3 object storage integration for large media assets
Utilize pre-signed URLs to bypass app server bandwidth bottlenecks
tradeoffs: App server file proxying: server CPU/bandwidth bottleneck vs Pre-signed S3 upload: direct low-cost client upload with short-lived token security
verificationQuestions: Why should not video files be stored directly in a SQL database table?
How does a pre-signed URL work to allow a client to upload directly to S3?

resources.title: Blob Storage and S3 Design Patterns

tasks.title: API Rate Limiting Algorithms & Distributed Redis Enforcers
tasks.description: Protect downstream microservices from abuse and DDoS using Rate Limiters. Compare Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket, and Sliding Window Counter algorithms enforced via Redis.
objectives: Select rate limiting algorithms based on burst traffic tolerance
Implement atomic distributed rate limiting counters in Redis
tradeoffs: Token Bucket: allows short traffic bursts vs Leaky Bucket: enforces strictly smooth constant output rate
verificationQuestions: Which rate limiting algorithm allows short bursty traffic while enforcing an average rate?
Why are atomic Lua scripts required when updating Redis rate limit counters?

tasks.title: Distributed Concurrency: Optimistic Locking & Atomic Redis Holds
tasks.description: Prevent race conditions and double-booking under extreme write contention. Compare Pessimistic locking (DB row locks), Optimistic locking (version numbers), and atomic Redis SETNX holds.
objectives: Prevent race conditions in high-concurrency write systems
Apply atomic Redis SETNX keys for temporary reservation holds
tradeoffs: Pessimistic DB lock: guarantees safety but destroys DB throughput under high contention vs Redis atomic hold: sub-ms fast failure rejection
verificationQuestions: Why does SELECT FOR UPDATE fail under 10,000 requests/sec seat reservation spikes?
How does Optimistic Locking with a version column detect concurrent updates?

tasks.title: Distributed Data Systems Architecture Milestone
tasks.description: Milestone: You have mastered distributed data tier building blocks including sharding, consistent hashing, queues, rate limiting, and distributed concurrency control.
objectives: Verify mastery across all core distributed building blocks

tasks.title: Step 1: Requirement Scoping & Functional vs Non-Functional Bounds
tasks.description: Lead the first 5 minutes of a System Design interview. Frame clear Functional Requirements (user actions) and Non-Functional Constraints (DAU, latency SLAs, availability 9s).
objectives: Structure requirement clarifying questions in minute 1 to 5 of an interview
Define non-functional availability (99.9% vs 99.99%) and latency SLAs
tradeoffs: Over-scoping: running out of time during interview vs Under-scoping: building the wrong architecture
verificationQuestions: What are 3 essential non-functional questions to ask for an event booking system?
What is the difference between functional and non-functional requirements?

tasks.title: Step 2: Back-of-the-Envelope Capacity Estimations
tasks.description: Perform rapid mental math calculations for Read/Write QPS, Peak QPS (2x-5x average), Storage Growth over 5 years, and Network Bandwidth bounds.
objectives: Calculate Average and Peak QPS from Daily Active Users (DAU)
Estimate 5-year data storage capacity in Terabytes
tradeoffs: Exact precision calculation: wastes valuable time vs Order-of-magnitude estimation: fast decision-making benchmark
verificationQuestions: If a system handles 10 Million DAU and each user makes 10 reads/day, what is the average Read QPS?
Why is Peak QPS critical for sizing load balancers and database capacity?

tasks.title: Step 3: API Contracts & High-Level Database Schema Design
tasks.description: Design RESTful API endpoint signatures (HTTP verbs, paths, payload parameters, idempotency keys) and define core database table schemas and primary keys.
objectives: Write clean REST API contracts with Idempotency-Key headers
Define core relational/NoSQL schemas with primary and foreign keys
tradeoffs: Generic endpoints: over-fetching data vs Focused REST resource endpoints: clean contract enforcement
verificationQuestions: Why should payment endpoints always require an Idempotency-Key header?
What fields belong in a User table vs a Reservation table?

resources.title: API Design and Data Modeling in Interviews

tasks.title: Step 4-6: High-Level Architecture, Deep Dives & Defense
tasks.description: Draw end-to-end architecture diagrams (Client -> Load Balancer -> API Gateway -> Services -> Redis -> DB), lead deep-dive bottleneck discussions, and defend trade-offs.
objectives: Construct high-level architecture diagrams seamlessly
Proactively identify bottlenecks and defend trade-off choices to interviewers
tradeoffs: Passive waiting for interviewer prompts vs Proactive driving of deep dives and trade-off defense
verificationQuestions: How do you pivot an interview smoothly from high-level diagram to deep-dive bottleneck?
What are 3 areas to cover during the final 3-minute wrap-up phase?

tasks.title: 6-Step Framework Mastery Self-Assessment
tasks.description: Execute a full verbal 45-minute walkthrough of the 6-step framework against a sample problem prompt, timing each phase strictly.
objectives: Validate strict adherence to the 45-minute interview time management framework

tasks.title: Case Study 1: Design a TinyURL / Bitly URL Shortener
tasks.description: Design a high-throughput key-value lookup service. Implement Base62 encoding, unique ID generation (Snowflake / pre-allocated ranges), Redis caching, and 301 vs 302 redirects.
objectives: Architect a scalable URL encoding service supporting 100M URLs/day
Compare 301 Permanent Redirect vs 302 Temporary Redirect HTTP codes
tradeoffs: 301 Redirect: browser caches redirect reducing server load but losing analytics vs 302 Redirect: server intercepts every click for full analytics
verificationQuestions: Why is Base62 (a-z, A-Z, 0-9) used for short URL hashes instead of Base64?
How does a pre-allocated ID range generator prevent duplicate short keys across nodes?

resources.title: System Design Primer: URL Shortener Solution

tasks.title: Worked Example & Diagram: URL Shortener Architecture
tasks.description: Draft the full architecture diagram and Python Base62 encoder/decoder pseudocode for the URL Shortener design.
objectives: Write clean Python pseudocode for Base62 encoding/decoding
Sketch the end-to-end data flow from short link click to long URL redirect

tasks.title: Case Study 2: Design Twitter / Facebook News Feed
tasks.description: Design a social newsfeed with high write fan-out. Master Fan-out on Write (Push model) vs Fan-out on Read (Pull model) and Hybrid approaches for celebrity accounts.
objectives: Architect hybrid Push/Pull news feed timeline generation
Solve celebrity user fan-out write bottlenecks
tradeoffs: Push model: sub-10ms fast read latency but high write cost on tweet posting vs Pull model: cheap write cost but high read query aggregation cost
verificationQuestions: Why does a pure Push model crash when an account with 80 million followers posts a tweet?
How does a Hybrid model treat regular users vs celebrity users differently?

tasks.title: Worked Example & Trade-off Practice: Social News Feed
tasks.description: Perform back-of-the-envelope calculations for 500M DAU newsfeed storage/bandwidth and sketch the Redis timeline cache data structures.
objectives: Calculate storage needed for 500M daily newsfeed users
Model Redis Sorted Sets (ZSET) for user timelines

tasks.title: Case Study 3: Design YouTube / Netflix Video Streaming
tasks.description: Architect a global video streaming platform. Master chunked video uploads, asynchronous transcoding pipeline workers, Blob storage (S3), and CDN adaptive bitrate streaming (HLS/DASH).
objectives: Design asynchronous video transcoding pipelines with message queues
Deliver adaptive bitrate video streaming via global CDN edge nodes
tradeoffs: Monolithic video storage: high buffering latency vs Adaptive chunked streaming: multi-resolution segment encoding for seamless playback on any device
verificationQuestions: Why are raw uploaded videos transcoded into multiple resolutions and chunked into 10-second segments?
How does adaptive bitrate streaming adjust video quality dynamically based on network speed?

tasks.title: Worked Example & Diagram: Video Streaming Platform
tasks.description: Construct the end-to-end architecture diagram showing S3 pre-signed upload, SQS queue, transcoding worker pool, and CDN playback flow.
objectives: Diagram the asynchronous video ingestion and distribution pipeline

tasks.title: Case Study 4: Design Ticketmaster Event Booking System
tasks.description: Design a high-concurrency event booking system with extreme write contention. Implement a Virtual Waiting Room, 10-minute temporary seat holds in Redis (SETNX), and Zero Double-Booking guarantees.
objectives: Eliminate double-booking during 100k QPS ticket drops
Implement 3-layer defense: Virtual Waiting Room -> Atomic Redis Hold -> Database Transaction
tradeoffs: Database row locking: DB crash under 100k QPS contention vs Atomic Redis Lua holds: instant sub-ms rejection for losing requests
verificationQuestions: How does an atomic Redis Lua script prevent two users from holding the same seat simultaneously?
What happens when a 10-minute temporary seat hold timer expires without payment?

tasks.title: Worked Example & Redis Lua Script: Ticketmaster Booking
tasks.description: Write the atomic Redis Lua reservation script and detail the database transaction logic with expiration sweeper background workers.
objectives: Write atomic seat reservation Redis Lua pseudocode
Design background expired reservation cleanup processes

tasks.title: Mock Practice 1: Complete 45-Min End-to-End System Design Run
tasks.description: Execute a full 45-minute timed mock interview walkthrough of an unannounced scenario (e.g. Rate Limiter or Distributed Cache). Document requirements, estimations, API, architecture, and trade-off defense.
objectives: Demonstrate complete 45-minute system design interview execution fluency

tasks.title: System Design Interview Readiness Final Milestone
tasks.description: Final Milestone: You are fully prepared to lead 45-minute Internship and New-Grad System Design technical interviews with structured confidence and clear trade-off defense.
objectives: Achieve full System Design technical interview readiness for Internship and New-Grad positions
